item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
hmmm, you're right. Radius limit would be a big nerf. I retract the suggestion.

But what I meant by "true nature" was its defining characteristic, that it is not what it appears to be. For example, the gaurd outside the door may know that there is an elephant in the room, but as long as he thinks it is just an elephant, there is no shift. But if he starts to get a clue that it might be something more than just a pacyderm, a shift is triggered. And if he deduces, perhaps by being a long-term gaurd, that 964 is something that changes, shifting would accelerate in direct proportion to his certainty. Which, now that I think about it, implies a positive-feedback loop and a source of constant containment breach threat.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
These are pertinent questions. I didn't go in much detail in description because I thought that it would detract too much from the main concept.

People at the current site don't know what is in the room. All on-site documentation on 964 is fabricated and says that it can walk through walls, bend steel, blow the heads with its thought and is memetic Japanese schoolgirl. So as long as 964 is none of those things everything should be fine.

If they hear an elephant in the containment chamber, it won't trigger reconstruction because this information is not sufficient to describe 964. As long as this elephant can't talk.

"distance clause" is actually quite big. Digital data at 200km mark will trigger reconstruction ~2 weeks after it's created.

Regarding long term-memory, protocol 964Δ6h takes care of that. I imagine it to be a nastier variation of amnesiacs, that not so much 'erases' as 'scrambles' memories, so that 964 will have to spend another month detecting them. Also, human memory is quite complex. Even if you walk into containment chamber and stare directly at 964, it will probably take around a hour before reconstruction starts. For comparison, written text from this distance will trigger it in under a minute.

Furthermore keep in mind that all this containment procedures and protocols a far from perfect. Despite all Foundation efforts new reconstruction occurs at least every two weeks, usually more often.

And it's okay to be confused. I wrote it, and I am still a little confused too.

item.content:encoded:
The concept is okay, DoD camouflage device that was uncontrollably succesful. But what I really like is the ingenious transport containment procedures. It changes to something other than what you think it is, so make sure everybody thinks it is dangerous and uncontainable. There's no way to know what form it will take, but it will be by definition something containable.

I agree with Dex. Maybe add a radius of effect limit. It can only detect information about itself within X meters, sort of thing. Alternatively, maybe tweak it so that it shifts when it detects data on its true nature rather than its current form. That way people can be aware of the obvious elephant in the room without necessarily triggering a change.
